Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

inshape 0.1.0

  • spells_to_panel() returns the units in the order they first appear in the data, as merge_spells() does, instead of sorted by the id columns; sort with dplyr::arrange() if needed. The spells are sorted on an integer id per unit, and sorting a character cpr was most of the time: on 2.5 million spells it went from 1.9 to about 1 second.

  • ensure_matched() hashes the keys of the data and the reference together instead of joining them (1.2 to 0.3 seconds on 4.5 million rows), and ensure_codes() with a temporal code list joins only the distinct pairs of code and time with the list (1.6 to 0.2 seconds). The rows reported are the same.

  • add_spell_status() converts the distinct periods to days, not the rows, and sorts the rows once for primo and ultimo.

  • describe_panel() on a database table works with dbplyr 2.6.0.

  • New violations() returns the rows that break a check: wrap the check in it, violations(ensure_unique(persons, cpr)). It replaces catching the inshape_failure condition by hand, where a check that passed handed back the whole data as if it were the violations.

  • A check that aborts (abort_msg) now shows the first rows as an aligned table. The columns were run together, because the message was formatted twice; a warning was not affected.

  • ensure_unique() and describe_key() stop when the key selects no columns, e.g. a starts_with() that matched nothing. The check passed before, with “Unique on” and no columns named.

  • Grouped data no longer adds its grouping columns to a key or an id: ensure_unique(group_by(df, year), cpr) checked year and cpr.

  • ensure_codes() takes time right after codes, before na_ok, as in describe_codes(). Name na_ok if it was passed by position.

  • ensure_matched() and ensure_valid_spells() name their columns in the default messages, as the other checkpoints do, and counts in failure messages have thousands separators.

  • Diagnostic columns in uniqueness, overlap and lifetime failures now get collision-safe names, preserving original columns in local and database violation sets.

  • describe_changes() reports shared list and matrix columns it cannot compare in columns_skipped and in the printed summary.

  • New ensure_valid_spells() checks missing starts and reversed boundaries, with open_end = FALSE to also reject missing ends.

  • ensure_codes() accepts temporal code lists with code, valid_from and valid_to, plus a time selection. Inclusive and open boundaries, multiple intervals and missing observation times have explicit rules.

  • New ensure_matched() checks coverage against a reference register, with composite and renamed keys and explicit missing-key matching. Both new checkpoints and temporal code checks support database and Arrow inputs.

  • First version. The key, panel and spell checks move here from expectr and are renamed so the two packages cannot be confused: expect_unique() is now ensure_unique(), expect_balanced() is ensure_balanced() and expect_no_overlap() is ensure_no_overlap(). A failure signals inshape_failure.

  • inshape is for interactive review of registers and writes nothing to disk: the offending rows are personal data. A failure shows the count and the first rows at the console and carries all of them on the condition, in memory. There is no log or dump argument, and no options: nothing is kept between calls either, and the engine runs on data.table’s threads. See “Personal data” in ?checkpoints.

  • New describe_key() and describe_panel() describe a key and a panel before a rule is chosen: duplicated keys split into exact copies and conflicts by column, and the panel’s units, gaps, entries, exits and participation patterns, in the spirit of Stata’s xtdescribe.

  • New describe_spells() relates each spell to the unit’s earlier spells: after a gap, adjacent (a transfer that may need merging), touching on one day, overlapping, nested or duplicate, and counts ongoing spells and spells that end before they start. ensure_no_overlap() shares its compiled pass over the sorted spells, and went from 6.0 to 2.8 seconds on 25 million spells.

  • New describe_changes() compares two extracts of a register by their key: keys that came and went, columns that came, went or changed type, and per column the values that changed, went missing or were filled in, the late corrections of a register without a time limit on them.

  • New describe_codes() shows how the codes of a column change over periods (first and last period, codes skipping periods, new and gone codes per period), on the panel engine, and ensure_codes() requires codes from a code list.

  • Every describe_*() function now takes a database or Arrow table and computes its summary in the database, fetching only the counts; the tests hold the numbers to those in memory.

  • New ensure_within() requires each row to lie within its unit’s lifetime: no observations after death or emigration, or before birth. A year compared with a date counts by the date’s year, and a missing bound is open. A compiled pass checks 25 million rows against birth and death dates in under half a second.

  • New merge_spells() merges spells recorded as several: back to back (transfers), overlapping, or less than max_gap days apart, optionally only when they agree in by columns such as the employer. It shares the compiled pass of describe_spells() and merges 25 million spells in about 5.5 seconds.

  • New describe_varying() shows which columns vary within units, and ensure_constant() requires columns such as sex or birth date to be constant within each unit; a missing value is not a contradiction. Both compare each row with its unit’s first value in one compiled pass; on 25 million rows ensure_constant(sex) takes 0.15 seconds.

  • Grouping by several key columns no longer fails when the product of their numbers of values passes the integer range.

  • A compiled grouping engine: keys are compressed to integer ids by a partitioned hash on data.table’s threads, and panels are checked as bit matrices. On 25 million rows ensure_balanced() went from 7.3 to 1.8 seconds and the grouping of a cpr column from 4.4 to 0.7.

  • spells_to_panel() and add_spell_status() move here from daos, unchanged.
